column1: # sorter_owner_requirements.tsv -- what a good sign-sorter page must do for the owner, in his words, one row per requirement.
# Started 9 Oct 2026 02:2x UTC by the account-3 orchestrator after the owner's mobile session (Harley 287 f.88r, Armstrong 1808)
# and his ask: "if you have the code for what a great sorter is we can just reuse. Instead of manually describing each time."
# Every row must become an automatic check (iPhone 13 + iPhone SE emulation) in the shared sorter recipe; a page that fails any
# row is not sent to the owner. Add a row (with date and the owner's words) every time he reports a sorter problem.

column2: The line strip is visible on an iPhone in the larger view (not a sliver)
column3: I can't see the strip at all. Mentioned this twice yesterday or day before. / "See, strip is borked"
column5: Harley 287 comments 01:57, 02:00 (also reported twice on 7-8 Oct)
column6: canvas CSS height >= 80 px on iPhone 13 and SE; strip pixels non-blank

column2: The larger view shows the lines above and below the sign
column3: I can't see above or below the symbol. There may be things worth seeing.
column6: context image includes >= 1 line height above and below the tile box (whole-page region or padded strips)

column2: A cut can be fixed in every direction, including onto the line above or below
column6: Fix the cut: drag/nudge each of top, bottom, left, right beyond the line band and Save; saved box differs as expected

column2: Question tiles ("Check these first" / "Most useful first") start already taken out, so one tap places each
column3: If they were already taken out I could put them in piles. Otherwise now I have to click on them to view them. Click to take out of this pile, then apply them to correct pile.
column6: page lands on step 2 with question tile 1 large; one tap on a pile card places it and advances; nothing saved until he acts

column2: ONE gesture rule on every page and in every box (piles, 'Check these first', 'Most useful first', tray): a single TAP takes the sign out into the 'to be decided' tray; a HOLD opens the sign's page large (on its line, with the answer buttons)
column3: If I hold on this I can move the piece. If I click on it once I'm taken into it / "Tap take out of pile, hold open symbol page" / "This is what I want. One tap it takes the symbol out and puts it in my tbd pile. If I hold on the symbol open [the] symbol page."
column5: Harley 287 comment 01:59; Armstrong 1808 comment 02:18; Armstrong 1808 comment 02:37 (the rule itself)
column6: iPhone 13 + SE emulation: tap a tile in each box -> it is in the tray and nothing else opened; hold a tile in each box -> the large view opens on its line; the page's hint text says exactly this; no box overrides it

column2: Pages already sent to the owner get every later fix (no stale versions)
column3: Why we make same mistakes over and over?
column6: registry of live sorter URLs; at each check-in every live page's template marker equals the current one or it is re-rendered and republished

column2: No colour-only cue that depends on red vs green (owner is red-green colour-blind)
column6: cvd_check (Machado deutan/protan) on every state pair; every state also has a shape/glyph/border cue
re-render keeps sids; a fixture with saved moves reloads with the same piles and no re-trayed decided tiles

column2: In a sign's card (opened by a hold), one finger sliding on the manuscript picture moves the view around the sign in any direction, like a map (a mouse drag on a desk; two fingers pinch the zoom); "Back to the sign" re-centres; the swipe to the next sign stays on the enlarged sign; Fix the cut still edits the box (a drag off the box moves the view)
column3: I wish when I clicked into a symbols page I could slide my finger on the manuscript surrounding my target symbol to see its surroundings. / "I marked a bunch a bad cut if when I clicked into it I couldn't move the manuscript to properly see around it or it didn't really display the full symbol."
column5: Bergh sign card, account-3 chat 11 Oct 00:0x UTC; Vivonne box check 10 Oct
column6: tools/sorter_preflight.py check 'pan' (iPhone 13: a drag 80 px left and 60 px down on a card's picture moves the view by the drag, the sign unchanged; tools/sign_sorter/browser_tests/test_pan.js --probe); the full test test_pan.js on the fixtures (iPhone 13, iPhone SE, desktop)

column2: In a sign's card on a desk, Ctrl + mouse wheel over the picture zooms it in and out around the pointer (a trackpad pinch too), one step of the Zoom slider per notch in the same range 1-8 with the slider moving with it, also while fixing a cut; the browser page itself does not zoom and a plain wheel still scrolls
column3: Allow me to ctrl+click + mouse scroll to zoom in and out so I can see more around the symbol in questions.
column6: tools/sign_sorter/browser_tests/test_wheel.js (desktop Chromium; lines.html, region.html, plain.html from make_fixtures.py): Ctrl + wheel up/down moves the slider by one, the wheel event is cancelled (no page zoom, visualViewport.scale 1), the point under the pointer stays within 2 css px on every axis not held at the sheet edge, the range ends hold, the window equals the slider's at that zoom, a pinch (small Ctrl wheel deltas) zooms 1-2 steps, a plain wheel is not cancelled and scrolls the card, Fix the cut stays on with the box unchanged

column2: The sign card walks the family it was opened in: from a pile tile (member, set-aside or waiting question) or "View larger", Left/Right keys, Previous/Next and a sideways swipe step through every sign shown under that family heading in on-screen order, stop at either end without wrapping and say so in words; after a move, set aside, bad cut, trash, keep, new sign or saved cut the card shows the next sign of the same family
column3: When I hit left or right keys while into one of the family, it moves to another symbol, but doesn't seem to be continuining in that family. I think it should ,then when you hit the end of that family unit it stops. So I the human can easily click through and knock out a whole family with new cuts or moves.
column5: Matignon f.110 sorter, account-3 chat 11 Oct 03:1x UTC
column6: tools/sign_sorter/browser_tests/test_family_nav.js (desktop keys + buttons, iPhone 13 swipes + taps; family.html and family_plain.html from make_fixtures.py): the card list equals the family tiles in DOM order across two piles with set-aside and waiting tiles; walks end-to-end; no wrap; end text "Last of N in family F"/"First sign in family F"; position "n of N in family F, pile P"; every decision shows the next sign of the fixed list; tray and "Check these first" cards keep their lists

column2: After a cut adjustment the sign must still be placeable: "when I make a cut adjustment it seems those symbols go somewhere as I am unable to place them in a pile" (owner, 14 Oct 2026 02:3x UTC, Vivonne f.201r page WAPAiDSVDwYjvDotTgBFhA: tiles f201r_L21_s2_01_007 and f201r_L22_s2_01_004 were recut, written to `checked` with pile unsorted, and never got a move -- both lost as unanswered)

Every pile shown to the person holds ONE sign, built from settled examples (label agrees with a known answer, or a sorted and applied pile), never from unsettled machine labels: "Each of the piles it showed had an intermix of symbols. So if I put something correct in there it may be marked incorrect as it is being compared against several symbols" (owner, 14 Oct 2026 02:4x UTC, Vivonne f.201r page WAPAiDSVDwYjvDotTgBFhA: the z pile was 8 of 8 3-shaped tiles; four of his placements followed those examples and were scored against the pile name). Scoring uses the pile name only, but a mixed pile misleads the choice.

Tiles reach the person well cut; a bad box is the page's fault, not the person's to fix: "although the cut was bad on some of them, I did not cut them" and "many of the piles have intermixed symbols that I can clearly see" (owner, 14 Oct 2026 03:0x UTC, attempt-2 page M1MRM2J7ZgF1VxCoqiJZgx, whose piles were already filtered to label-agrees-with-truth tiles: the machine label inventory itself merges glyphs, so a label-defined pile mixes shapes even when every member is "correct")

The sign being asked about is never shown a second time in a way that reads as a duplicate in another pile; the waiting sign and the pile exemplars are visibly different things (a frame, a label "this sign", or the waiting sign hidden from the unsorted preview), and two piles whose codes share one meaning (s and z both read "a" in this key) are told apart on the page or merged, since truth-consistency alone cannot separate them: "i see a symbol in multiple piles" (owner, 15 Oct 2026 00:4x UTC, Vivonne f.191r packet Q01: the waiting tile f191r_L13_s2_01_020 in the unsorted preview beside a look-alike known-answer tile in pile z; the z pile itself holds a z-shape, an x-shape and 3-shapes from the readers' merged label, R13/R14 again).

The person is never asked to fix a cut: the page asks for one thing, "which pile holds signs that look like this one", judged from the sign shown in its own line (the strip with the bracket), and a box so wrong that the sign cannot be told even there gets "Bad cut" and nothing else; "Fix the cut" is withdrawn from the question page until R12 is fixed and shown fixed on a test tile, because the defect recurred on the second page version: "when i fix the cut the symbol disappears ... So is the objective to have me just place what I see as best I can? Or is it to have the cuts etc. fixed as I see them and placed were they go? Cause I think we are making things unnecessarily complicated." (owner, 15 Oct 2026 01:2x UTC, Vivonne f.191r packet; the recut itself was saved to the recuts collection for f191r_L10_s1_01_020, so the data survives even when the page hides the tile).
